body.statement: For every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) in the no-selection overlap satisfying \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\), the simultaneous equations in the proof of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1 on pages 12135--12137 identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\). If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, its atlas value agrees with \(\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K})\). Kawakami's identified scope is the four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types, together with their treatment-conditional weights used for PN and PS, under Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii). For the single explicit selected boundary datum \((p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\), \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\), but \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular for each \(x\): because \(\mathcal W=\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}\), its first column is the sum of its last three columns. Thus this legal selected response-cycle law violates the named invertibility assumption in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i) while remaining classified by the atlas; this is a strict scope separation, not a subsumption claim.
body.justification: This supporting theorem records the exact no-selection IV-plus-proxy overlap and a one-law separation from Kawakami's regular invertibility domain.
body.gap: Kawakami (2021), Figure 2(b), equation (2), Theorem 1(i)--(iii), and its appendix identify all four response-type probabilities under invertible proxy-loading and observable blocks plus cross-treatment separation, but do not classify selected or singular response-cycle fibers.
body.consumer: IV-plus-proxy analysts can audit agreement on Kawakami-regular laws and recognize a concrete selected boundary law for which the regular matrix method is unavailable but the atlas still returns an exact certificate.
